summary: The note describes how public health campaigns fight substance abuse by combining prevention and rehabilitation. It explains addiction as a brain disease, then covers campaigns for youth education, stigma reduction, rehab, app-based support, and social safety net programs. It argues these parts form an integrated strategy grounded in science and compassion.
one_line: Overview of public health campaigns against substance abuse that combine prevention, stigma reduction, rehabilitation, technology, and social support, grounded in addiction science.
key_facts: Dr. Elizabeth Martinez, a neuroscientist specializing in addiction biology, shared insights at a webinar on September 5, 2023, describing addiction as a complex brain disease marked by compulsive substance seeking and use despite harmful consequences.
Repeated substance use alters the brain's reward system and rewires neurotransmitters and neural pathways, so addiction often requires medical intervention, much like diabetes or heart disease.
The "Catch Them Before It Starts" campaign, spearheaded by the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA), was launched on October 12, 2023 to educate young people about substance abuse.

Dr. John Carter, a health education specialist, and his team visit schools, community centers, and online platforms to teach about the dangers of substance abuse through seminars, workshops, and social media campaigns.
The "Speak Up, Speak Out" campaign, circulating since January 2024, aims to break the silence and shame around addiction and normalize seeking help.
Local celebrity Marcus Greene is among public figures who have shared their own struggles with substance use in the "Speak Up, Speak Out" campaign.
Therapist Rachel Thompson noted significant increases in people signing up for counselling sessions or support groups as the stigma-reduction campaign gained traction.
The "Road to Recovery" campaign launched on November 2, 2023 and highlights rehabilitation programs, which include therapy, medication, support groups, and aftercare beyond detox.
The "Phoenix Pathway" rehabilitation center uses neuroscience, psychology, cognitive-behavioral therapy, and mindfulness, and claims a success rate well above average.
The "Connect for Recovery" campaign launched its app on September 25, 2023, with a helpline, a chat function with licensed counselors, and a database of nearby support groups and rehab facilities.
The Connect for Recovery app uses data-driven algorithms to provide personalized support suggestions and follow-up plans for people in recovery.
The "Sustain Sobriety" initiative opened on December 15, 2023 and works with workplaces, community leaders, and federal programs on job training, education, and housing to prevent relapse.
